title: Nourishing Algerian Kinako Tagine
description: A fragrant, resinous tagine that blends traditional Algerian spices with nutty kinako, slow‑cooked in a nimono‑style simmer for an energizing, halal‑friendly meal.
instructions: Wash and pat dry the chicken thighs; season both sides with salt, pepper, cumin, coriander, and paprika.
Heat the olive oil in a wide, heavy‑bottomed pot over medium heat; brown the chicken thighs on all sides, about 5 minutes per side, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot add the chopped onion and minced garlic; sauté until the onion becomes translucent, about 4 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pot and pour in enough water to almost cover the meat; bring to a gentle simmer and cover, simmering for 35 minutes.
While the chicken simmers, toast the chopped apricots in a dry skillet until they soften and become slightly caramelized, about 3 minutes.
Stir the kinako into the simmering liquid, whisking until fully dissolved; add the toasted apricots and lemon zest.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and let the tagine finish cooking for an additional 10 minutes so the flavors meld.
Taste the broth; adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Arrange the cooked chicken on a serving platter and pour the sauce and apricots over it.
Garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro if desired and serve hot with couscous or crusty bread.
